learning_outcomes.text: Students should be able to name, explain, and apply the covered fundamentals and applications of materials science and the most important material testing procedures in practical operations.

syllabus_topics: MATERIALS SCIENCE: Types of bonding, atomic arrangement, polymorphism, crystal lattice defects
Physical and mechanical properties of materials: thermal expansion, electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, elastic behavior
Thermally activated processes: diffusion, recovery and recrystallization, creep and stress relaxation
Alloy formation and phase diagrams: lens diagram, eutectic, peritectic, systems with compound formation
Iron-carbon phase diagram: pure iron, stable system, metastable system
Steel production
Standard-compliant designation of ferrous materials
Heat treatment of steels: temperature control, normal annealing, soft annealing, stress-relief annealing, hardening, CCT diagrams, hardening processes, tempering, surface hardening
Steel groups: effect of carbon and alloying elements, structural steels, heat-treatable steels, heat-resistant steels, cold-tough steels, stainless steels, tool steels
Cast iron materials: cast steel, cast iron
Non-ferrous metals: standard-compliant designation, aluminum and alloys, precipitation hardening
Fundamentals of lightweight construction characteristics
Other non-ferrous metals and inorganic non-metallic materials: glass, ceramics (structure, production, properties)
Plastics: definition, production, structure, properties
MATERIALS TESTING: Tensile test: testing equipment, specimens, stress-strain diagram, material properties
Hardness testing: Brinell, Vickers, and Rockwell testing, comparison of methods
Impact test: fundamentals, testing equipment, test procedure, influence of material and temperature, practical significance
Fatigue testing: processes in the microstructure, fracture surface, Wöhler curve
Metallography: macroscopic methods, microscopic methods, scanning electron microscopy
Non-destructive testing: dye penetrant testing, magnetic and inductive methods, ultrasonic testing, radiographic testing

LABORATORY EXPERIMENTS: In the laboratory, tensile tests, hardness testing procedures, impact testing, metallography, scanning electron microscopy are demonstrated and evaluated with student participation.
assessment_rules: The assessment includes a 120-minute written exam and a preliminary examination requirement for laboratory work. The laboratory work is a prerequisite for taking the exam.
